Hi Neha — thanks for the updated MSA and order form PDF. A few questions surfaced after our procurement review: 

1) The auto-renew language in Section 2.3 looks like annual automatic renewal unless notice given 60 days before term end. We were expecting 30 days. Can you confirm whether 60 is firm or negotiable?
2) Termination for convenience: OrbitCloud prefers a 90-day notice and an option for a pro-rated refund of prepaid committed capacity. Current draft says 120 days and no refunds.
3) Sunset/offboarding: we need a clear runbook for data handoff and an SLA for support during the offboard window (30 days). Can you attach any operational playbook?

We have our procurement lead CC'd — Maya (m.castillo@orbitcloud.com). Happy to hop on 30-min call tomorrow to accelerate.

Thanks Evan — good questions. Quick summary of Redwood's position and suggested compromise below; I've attached a redline (Redwood_MSA_Redline_v3.docx) that tracks these changes. We can take the rest to legal if you like.

- Auto-renew: We prefer the 60-day notice to ensure operational handoffs and invoicing cutovers don't create gaps. That said, for pilot customers (<= $75k ARR) we will accept a 30-day notice. For enterprise (like OrbitCloud) we can agree to 45-day notice as a middle ground. Proposed: change to 45 days and include a one-time exception for pilot-to-enterprise conversion.

- Termination for convenience: Redwood's standard is 120 days to allow reserved GPU capacity to be reallocated and to avoid sudden billing cliffs. We can offer a 90-day notice in exchange for either (a) a pro-rata refund on unused prepayments capped at 25% of remaining committed spend, or (b) a 90-day termination fee equal to 50% of the remaining committed monthly run-rate — OrbitCloud to choose. This preserves economics while offering OrbitCloud flexibility.

- Offboard/runbook: attaching Offboard_Runbook_v1.xlsx with a 30-day operational handoff checklist and data export timelines. We will commit to a 30-day support SLA during the offboard window (Tier-2 response within 4 hours; weekly check-ins).

If that sounds reasonable I can loop legal (Karthik and Marissa) to finalize redlines and provide a DocuSign envelope. If you want changes to the refund cap or fee mechanics, call tomorrow 10am PT works for me.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding OrbitCloud thread. Highlights we need Legal to weigh in on:

- 45-day compromise for auto-renew is okay commercial, but legal should confirm any downstream billing implications and how notices are delivered (email vs registered mail).
- Termination option: commercial is suggesting either refund cap (25%) or termination fee (50% remaining run-rate). We should compute the math for a sample commitment (OrbitCloud TCV $600k, remaining $360k) to see impact.
- Offboard SLA: operations can commit to 30-day support and weekly check-ins, but we should add a clause limiting liability for third-party integrations.

Marissa / Karthik — can you review the redline and call out any clauses you want tightened (notice delivery, refund calculation, limitation of liability during offboard)? Laura, can you confirm whether Finance is okay with a 25% pro-rata cap vs a straight termination fee?

Thanks,

Evan / Maya — thanks for the note and the patience. Karthik and I reviewed the redline and we can accept the commercial compromises Neha outlined with the following legal specifics to be reflected in the attached redline before signature: 

1) Notice mechanics: specify that termination or non-renewal notice must be given via email to legal@redwood.com and procurement@orbitcloud.com, with a copy via registered mail to the addresses listed in Schedule A. Effective date is the date received by Redwood's legal email.
2) Refund calc: pro-rata refund is based on unused pre-paid committed capacity, calculated at the monthly committed rate. The 25% cap applies to the total remaining committed spend, not per-month.
3) Limitation of liability: add carveout that Redwood's offboard support excludes remediation for third-party vendor failures and that professional services for complex data migration will be provided on a time-and-materials basis.
4) Transition support SLA: confirm the 30-day dedicated support window and add a single 30-day extension option if both parties agree in writing.

If OrbitCloud accepts the redline wording above, we will send a final DocuSign link this afternoon and copy Finance for final billing setup (Laura). Evan — please confirm which commercial option you prefer (25% pro-rata refund vs 50% termination fee) so we can lock numbers.

Best,
